intent.raw_query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January 2026

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep
experiences.description: Join a guided super jeep tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from city light pollution for the best chance of witnessing the Aurora Borealis. Expert guides track solar activity and cloud cover to find the clearest skies, and you'll learn about the science and folklore behind the lights.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in Iceland's most iconic milky-blue geothermal pool surrounded by black lava fields. The mineral-rich waters average 38–40°C and are renowned for skin benefits. Book the Comfort package to include a silica mud mask and a drink at the in-water bar.
experiences.best_time_of_day: Evening (for potential northern lights views overhead)

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring dating to 1891 set in a geothermal field with bubbling mud pots and small geysers. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic local experience costs a fraction of the price and feels genuinely wild.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore the colorful streets of downtown Reykjavik with a local guide, sampling traditional Icelandic dishes like skyr, lamb soup (kjötsúpa), fresh langoustine, and rye bread baked in geothermal ground. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church and the Harpa Concert Hall along the way.

experiences.name: Glacier Hike on Sólheimajökull
experiences.description: Strap on crampons and hike across the stunning Sólheimajökull glacier outlet with a certified guide. Marvel at ice caves, crevasses, and vivid blue ice formations while learning about Iceland's glacial geology and climate change. A truly unforgettable physical adventure on the South Coast.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs and collect luggage. Take the budget-friendly Flybus shuttle (approx. 3,500 ISK) to Reykjavik area and check into Aegean Bliss Resort. Get settled and rest after your journey.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the airport Subway or 10-11 convenience store near the hotel (budget-friendly, under 1,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the Flybus shuttle online for a slight discount. Exchange some currency or use ATMs at the airport. January in Iceland means very limited daylight (around 5 hours), temperatures near 0°C, and excellent chances for northern lights viewing. Pack warm layers immediately upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from jet lag. Enjoy a slow morning at the hotel. Walk along the nearby beachfront area to get your bearings and take in the dramatic Icelandic winter coastline. Sunrise won't occur until around 11:00 AM in January, so there's no rush.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into Reykjavik city center (bus or walk depending on hotel location). Visit the iconic Hallgrimskirkja church (exterior free, tower entry ~1,000 ISK). Stroll down Laugavegur street, window shop, and explore the colorful corrugated iron houses. Visit Harpa Concert Hall exterior and waterfront for free.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights hunt begins! Check aurora forecast at vedur.is (free). Head to a dark spot near the coast or Grótta Lighthouse (free, walkable from Reykjavik) for your first northern lights attempt. Dress in maximum layers.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or pick up skyr yogurt and bread from Bonus supermarket (Iceland's cheapest grocery chain, under 800 ISK)
meals.lunch: Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur - Iceland's famous hot dog stand in Reykjavik, one hot dog costs ~500 ISK. A true budget Icelandic experience.
meals.dinner: Hlöllabátar (Subway-style sandwich shop) on Laugavegur, around 1,800-2,200 ISK for a filling meal

day_by_day.notes: Buy a multi-day Strætó bus pass for getting around Reykjavik cheaply. Download the Strætó app for bus routes. Stock up on groceries at Bonus (yellow pig logo) for the cheapest prices in Iceland.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the famous Reykjavik Flea Market (Kolaportið) if open on weekends, otherwise explore the Settlement Exhibition Museum (around 1,800 ISK) to learn about Viking-age Reykjavik. Walk to Tjörnin pond to see birds and the colorful city hall.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a self-guided walking tour of Reykjavik's street art scene (completely free). Visit the National Museum of Iceland (2,000 ISK, free for under 18s) for a deep dive into Icelandic history and culture. Browse the Kolaportið flea market for budget souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights hunting session. Take a free self-drive or walk to Öskjuhlíð hill near Perlan for an elevated dark viewing spot. Alternatively, join a budget group northern lights bus tour (approx. 5,000-7,000 ISK) which includes transportation to darker areas.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered from Bonus supermarket - oatmeal, skyr, and coffee (under 600 ISK)
meals.lunch: Reykjavik Roasters cafe for coffee and a pastry, or pick up a sandwich from a supermarket (under 1,200 ISK)
meals.dinner: Cook a simple pasta meal in hotel kitchen if available, or try Aktu Taktu fast food restaurant for budget burgers around 1,500-2,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: January aurora forecast: KP index of 3 or above gives good viewing chances. Always check cloud cover - clear skies are essential. The aurora forecast website vedur.is is your best free tool.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip preparation: Pack snacks and thermos of hot drink. Drive or join a budget tour to the Golden Circle. Start with Þingvellir National Park (free entry) - walk the rift valley between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates. Explore the Almannagjá gorge and Öxará river area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue Golden Circle: Visit the Geysir geothermal area (free to walk around) and watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5-10 minutes shooting water 20-30 meters high. Then head to Gullfoss waterfall (free entry) - one of Iceland's most spectacular waterfalls, especially dramatic in winter with ice formations.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward Reykjavik. Stop at Kerið volcanic crater lake (350 ISK entry) if time permits - stunning in winter. Check aurora forecast and head to a dark rural area on the way back for northern lights viewing. The Golden Circle route offers excellent dark sky opportunities.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast at hotel before departure (pack extra snacks for the day)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from supermarket - sandwiches, fruit, and hot drink in thermos (saves significant money vs. tourist area restaurants)
meals.dinner: Upon return to Reykjavik, try Noodle Station on Laugavegur for warming ramen soup around 1,800 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Renting a car for the Golden Circle costs around 8,000-12,000 ISK per day for a small car. Split with fellow travelers to reduce costs. Alternatively, join a budget group day tour for around 8,000-10,000 ISK which includes transportation. Roads may be icy - drive carefully and check road.is for conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Blue Lagoon area (book well in advance - entry from 9,990 ISK for Comfort package). Soak in the famous geothermal hot spring spa with its milky blue mineral-rich waters. The silica mud masks are included and great for skin. Arrive early to avoid crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue soaking and relaxing at the Blue Lagoon. Explore the surrounding lava field landscape. The steam rising from the lagoon in cold January air creates a magical atmosphere. Take photos of the dramatic contrast between the blue water and dark lava rocks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to hotel and rest after a relaxing spa day. Check aurora forecast for evening viewing. If aurora is forecasted, drive or walk to the nearest dark beach area near the hotel for viewing. The beachfront hotel location may offer good northern lights viewing from the shore itself.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast before Blue Lagoon departure
meals.lunch: LAVA Restaurant inside Blue Lagoon is expensive - instead pack your own snacks or eat the included light snack (some packages include a drink). Eat before or after.
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner from Bonus supermarket - cook simple meal or enjoy bread, cheese, and deli items (under 1,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Blue Lagoon is the biggest splurge of the trip but worth it for the unique experience. Book months in advance as it sells out, especially in winter. The Comfort package is the most budget-friendly option. Bring flip-flops and your own towel if possible to avoid rental fees.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Reykjanes Peninsula (near the hotel if staying in that area). Visit the Bridge Between Continents (free) - a small footbridge symbolizing the gap between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates. Walk the dramatic lava fields and coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Reykjanesviti lighthouse (free) - Iceland's oldest lighthouse surrounded by dramatic geothermal activity, boiling mud pools, and fumaroles. Walk the marked trails around the geothermal area. Visit Gunnuhver hot spring area with its powerful steam vents (free).
day_by_day.evening: Drive to a remote dark area on the Reykjanes Peninsula for northern lights hunting. The peninsula's sparse population means very dark skies. Set up on a beach or hilltop and wait for aurora activity. Bring hot drinks and warm blankets.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel - skyr, fruit, and instant coffee
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch for the peninsula exploration - sandwiches and thermos of soup
meals.dinner: Return to Reykjavik for dinner at Sægreifinn (The Sea Baron) for budget lobster soup around 1,500 ISK - a Reykjavik institution

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjanes Peninsula is geologically one of the most active areas in Iceland. Check for any volcanic activity alerts before visiting. The area around Svartsengi and Grindavik has seen recent eruptions - always check safetravel.is for current conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Rest day and mid-trip recovery. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely morning. Visit a local geothermal public swimming pool (Sundlaug) - Laugardalslaug in Reykjavik is the largest (around 1,000 ISK entry) with hot tubs, steam rooms, and outdoor pools. This is how locals relax.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Laugardalur valley area - visit the free botanical garden (winter hours limited but gardens are still beautiful in snow). Walk around the area and visit the Ásmundur Sveinsson Sculpture Museum exterior (free outdoor sculptures). Browse local shops.
day_by_day.evening: Northern lights viewing from Grótta Lighthouse peninsula - one of the best free viewing spots near Reykjavik. The lighthouse sits on a small tidal island accessible at low tide. Check tide times before visiting. Bring a tripod for aurora photography.

meals.breakfast: Treat yourself to breakfast at Sandholt Bakery on Laugavegur - fresh pastries and coffee around 1,500 ISK
meals.lunch: Supermarket lunch - pick up ready-made soup or sandwiches from Krónan or Bónus
meals.dinner: Cook a full meal at the hotel if kitchen available, or try Kebabhúsið for affordable kebabs around 1,500-1,800 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Geothermal public pools are a quintessential Icelandic experience and very budget-friendly. Icelanders use them daily for socializing. Follow pool etiquette: shower thoroughly without swimsuit before entering. January is perfect for outdoor hot tub soaking while snow may be falling.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to South Iceland: Depart early for Seljalandsfoss waterfall (free, parking fee ~750 ISK). In summer you can walk behind it, but in January the path may be icy and closed - check conditions. The waterfall is stunning with ice formations in winter. Continue to Skógafoss waterfall (free) - equally impressive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Dyrhólaey peninsula (free) for dramatic coastal views and the iconic rock arch over the sea. Continue to Reynisfjara black sand beach (free) - one of the most dramatic beaches in the world with basalt column formations and powerful Atlantic waves. Exercise extreme caution - sneaker waves are deadly here.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Reykjavik along Route 1. Stop at any dark rural area for northern lights viewing on the way back. The south coast road offers vast open skies perfect for aurora hunting. Return to hotel.

meals.breakfast: Very early self-catered breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Pack substantial lunch from supermarket - the south coast has limited budget dining options
meals.dinner: Back in Reykjavik, try Ísbúð Vesturbæjar ice cream parlor (yes, Icelanders eat ice cream in winter!) then a budget meal at Hlöllabátar

day_by_day.notes: The south coast road can be treacherous in January. Check road.is and weather forecasts before departing. Rental car with 4WD recommended for winter driving. NEVER turn your back on the ocean at Reynisfjara - people have died from sneaker waves. Stay behind the safety markers.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Perlan museum (exterior free, museum entry around 3,990 ISK but optional). Walk around the Öskjuhlíð hill and forest area for free panoramic views of Reykjavik and the surrounding mountains and ocean. On clear days, you can see across to the Snæfellsjökull glacier.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the 101 Reykjavik neighborhood in depth. Visit the Volcano House museum (2,500 ISK) for fascinating documentary films about Iceland's volcanic eruptions. Browse the Kolaportið flea market if open. Visit Austurvöllur square and the Alþingi parliament building exterior.
day_by_day.evening: Free aurora hunting evening. Drive or take a bus to Þingvellir National Park (about 45 minutes from Reykjavik) for some of Iceland's darkest skies near the capital. The park is free and open 24 hours. Bring warm sleeping bags to lie on and watch the sky.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Cheap and cheerful: Icelandic hot dogs at Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur again - a must-have multiple times during the trip
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer budget meal at Grillmarkadurinn's happy hour or try Forréttabarinn for small plates around 2,500-3,500 ISK

day_by_day.notes: January 23rd - you're past the midpoint of the trip. Review your spending and adjust if needed. The aurora season is at its peak in January with up to 17-18 hours of darkness providing maximum viewing opportunities. Keep checking the aurora forecast daily.

day_by_day.morning: Snæfellsnes Peninsula day trip (long day - depart very early). Drive approximately 2.5 hours to reach the peninsula. Visit Snæfellsjökull glacier volcano (the setting of Jules Verne's Journey to the Center of the Earth). The glacier is visible from a distance - getting close requires a guided tour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Snæfellsnes: Visit Arnarstapi coastal village with dramatic basalt cliffs and lava arch (free). Walk the marked trail between Arnarstapi and Hellnar along the cliff tops (about 2.5km, free). Visit Kirkjufell mountain - Iceland's most photographed mountain - and Kirkjufellsfoss waterfall (free).
day_by_day.evening: The drive back along the Snæfellsnes Peninsula offers excellent northern lights viewing opportunities away from city lights. Stop at multiple dark spots on the way back. Return to hotel late evening.

meals.breakfast: Very early packed breakfast before 6 AM departure
meals.lunch: Pack a substantial lunch and snacks - limited budget options on the peninsula
meals.dinner: Late dinner upon return - grab something from a 24-hour convenience store like 10-11 or Krónan, or heat up pre-bought supermarket food

day_by_day.notes: This is a very long day (potentially 12+ hours of driving and exploring). The Snæfellsnes Peninsula is one of Iceland's most diverse and beautiful regions. Consider whether to rent a car specifically for this day or join a budget group tour. Road conditions in January can be challenging on the peninsula.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery morning after the long Snæfellsnes day. Visit Nauthólsvík geothermal beach (free in winter) - a small sheltered bay where geothermally heated water creates a warmer swimming area. Brave Icelanders swim here year-round. Walk along the beach and enjoy the surreal experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free National Gallery of Iceland (Listasafn Íslands) for Icelandic and international art. Walk through the Grandi harbor area - Reykjavik's up-and-coming creative district with street art, the Marshall House arts center, and the Reykjavik Maritime Museum (around 1,800 ISK). Browse the Farmers Market concept store.
day_by_day.evening: Final serious northern lights hunting night. Join a budget aurora tour if you haven't seen them clearly yet (5,000-8,000 ISK for group tours). Many tours offer a second free trip if aurora isn't visible. Head to the darkest possible location. This is one of your last chances.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely self-catered breakfast at hotel
meals.lunch: Matur og Drykkur for traditional Icelandic lunch (slightly pricier at 2,500-3,500 ISK but worth it for authentic experience)
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner from supermarket to save money for the aurora tour

day_by_day.notes: If you haven't seen the northern lights yet, don't give up - January is statistically one of the best months. Cloud cover is the main enemy. Consider driving north of Reykjavik toward Borgarnes for potentially clearer skies if Reykjavik area is cloudy.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Árbæjarsafn Open Air Museum (around 1,800 ISK) - an outdoor museum of historic Icelandic buildings and farm life. Walk through reconstructed turf houses and learn about how Icelanders lived historically. The winter setting adds atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Souvenir shopping on a budget: Visit Kolaportið flea market for the cheapest souvenirs (Icelandic wool items, vintage items). Browse Laugavegur street. Visit Vikurprjón for authentic Icelandic lopapeysa wool sweaters (expensive new, but look for second-hand options at the flea market).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell northern lights attempt and final evening in Iceland. Visit Seltjarnarnes peninsula tip (free) for a final aurora viewing session. Then enjoy a farewell dinner in Reykjavik. Reflect on the trip and pack for departure.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Budget lunch at Reykjavik's food halls or a supermarket meal
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Snaps Bistro Bar or Cafe Loki (traditional Icelandic food including hákarl fermented shark if you're brave) around 2,500-3,500 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Start packing this evening. Check airline baggage requirements. If you bought Icelandic wool items, they can be bulky. Keep receipts for VAT refund at the airport (available on purchases over 6,000 ISK from registered shops - can save 15-20% back). Leave extra time tomorrow for airport processes.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. If time permits before airport transfer, take one last walk along the beachfront to soak in the Icelandic coastal scenery. Watch for the late sunrise (around 11:00 AM) painting the sky in golden winter light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Keflavik International Airport. Allow at least 2.5-3 hours before departure for check-in, security, and VAT refund processing. Complete VAT refund paperwork at the airport for eligible purchases. Browse duty-free for any last-minute Icelandic products (Brennivín schnapps, Icelandic chocolate, skyr).
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Reflect on an incredible 13-day budget adventure through Iceland featuring geothermal hot springs, dramatic winter landscapes, and hopefully spectacular northern lights displays.

meals.breakfast: Final self-catered breakfast at hotel or grab something quick before checkout
meals.lunch: Airport food (budget for around 2,000-2,500 ISK for airport prices) or eat before arriving at the airport
meals.dinner: On the plane

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary tips: Total estimated budget for 13 days (excluding flights and accommodation) approximately 150,000-200,000 ISK (~$1,100-$1,500 USD) covering food, local transport, activities, and car rental days. Biggest savings came from: Bonus supermarket meals, packed lunches for day trips, free natural attractions, and public buses in Reykjavik. Iceland is expensive but very manageable on a budget with planning.

trip_options.title: Classic Iceland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront accommodation. If the sky is clear, step outside briefly — January nights in Iceland offer a chance to spot the Northern Lights right from the resort.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight
meals.lunch: N/A — in-flight
meals.dinner: Grab a light snack at the airport arrivals hall or a convenience item from the resort's welcome amenities upon check-in

day_by_day.notes: Flight arrives at 22:30 local time. January in Iceland means darkness for roughly 19–20 hours per day — ideal for Northern Lights viewing. Keep aurora alert apps (e.g., Vedur.is) downloaded and notifications on throughout the trip. Pack warm layers for the transfer.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a short walk along the beachfront to acclimate to Iceland's dramatic winter landscape — dark volcanic sand, crashing Atlantic waves, and crisp Arctic air. Pick up a local SIM card or confirm data roaming for navigation throughout the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into Reykjavik (approx. 40–50 min drive from the resort area) for the Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour. Explore the colorful streets of downtown Reykjavik with a local guide, sampling traditional Icelandic bites including skyr, lamb soup, rye bread, and local cheeses. Visit iconic landmarks like Hallgrímskirkja church and the Sun Voyager sculpture along the way.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll Laugavegur Street for window shopping and atmosphere as evening darkness falls by mid-afternoon. Dine at a mid-range restaurant in downtown Reykjavik before returning to the resort. Keep an eye on aurora forecasts — if KP index is favorable, the drive back along the coast may offer a spectacular light show.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast buffet at Aegean Bliss Resort — included or à la carte mid-range option
meals.lunch: Tastings included during the Food & Culture Walking Tour; supplement with a bowl of Icelandic lamb soup (kjötsúpa) at a local café (~2,500–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Grillið or Bergsson Mathús in Reykjavik — expect 4,000–7,000 ISK per person for a hearty Icelandic main course with local fish or lamb

day_by_day.notes: Book the Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour in advance online. Tours typically run early afternoon in winter. Wear waterproof boots and layered clothing — January temperatures average -1°C to 3°C with wind chill making it feel colder.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa (only 20 minutes from the Reykjanes Peninsula area near the resort). Arrive early for the first entry slot to beat crowds. Soak in Iceland's iconic milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica, algae, and minerals. Apply the complimentary silica mud mask and enjoy the steam caves. The contrast of steaming warm water against January's icy air and possible snow is magical.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue soaking or use the Blue Lagoon's sauna and steam facilities. Enjoy a mid-afternoon snack at the lagoon's in-water bar (included with some packages). Depart by early afternoon and return to the resort to rest and warm up. Use the quiet hours to plan the coming days and review aurora forecasts.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep — join a guided super jeep tour departing from the Reykjavik/Reykjanes area into the Icelandic wilderness, far from city light pollution. Expert guides use real-time aurora and cloud-cover data to find the best viewing locations. Wrap up in blankets and witness the dancing green and purple curtains of the aurora borealis overhead.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departing for the Blue Lagoon — pack a snack for the car
meals.lunch: Light meal at the Blue Lagoon's Lava Restaurant or grab a soup and bread from the lagoon café (~3,500–5,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Warm up after the Northern Lights tour with a hearty dinner back near the resort or in a nearby town — try a local grill house for lamb chops or fish stew (~4,500–6,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Blue Lagoon entry well in advance — slots sell out weeks ahead, especially in winter. Book the Northern Lights Super Jeep tour for the evening; tours typically run 21:00–01:00. Northern Lights sightings are never guaranteed but January offers long dark hours maximizing chances.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning following the late Northern Lights tour. Sleep in, enjoy a slow breakfast at the resort. Review photos and footage from last night. Check aurora forecasts and road conditions (road.is) for the coming days. Begin planning the Golden Circle day trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Self-drive or join a guided Golden Circle tour: Visit Þingvellir National Park (UNESCO World Heritage Site) where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Walk through Almannagjá canyon and learn about Iceland's ancient parliament. Continue to the Geysir Geothermal Area to watch Strokkur erupt every 5–10 minutes shooting boiling water 30 meters into the air.
day_by_day.evening: Complete the Golden Circle with a visit to Gullfoss Waterfall — Iceland's most famous two-tiered cascade. In winter, the falls are often partially frozen and draped in ice formations. Return to the resort via the southern route. If skies are clear, pull over on a dark stretch of road for an impromptu aurora watch.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — take your time
meals.lunch: Café Geysir near the Geysir area — hearty lamb soup or a sandwich (~2,500–4,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Farmhouse-style dinner at Friðheimar Tomato Farm Restaurant (on the Golden Circle route) — unique greenhouse dining with tomato-based menu items (~5,000–7,000 ISK); reserve ahead

day_by_day.notes: Golden Circle is approximately 300 km round trip from the Reykjanes area — allow a full afternoon and evening. Roads are generally well-maintained but check conditions on road.is before departing. Sunset occurs around 11:30 and darkness falls by 15:30 in January, so all Golden Circle sights will be experienced in low light or darkness — bring a headlamp.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east along the South Coast — one of Iceland's most scenic drives. First stop: Seljalandsfoss Waterfall, where you can walk behind the curtain of falling water (may be icy/closed in winter — check conditions). Continue to Skógafoss Waterfall, a massive 60-meter cascade with a rainbow often visible in the mist. Climb the staircase alongside for elevated views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Sólheimajökull Glacier for a guided Glacier Hike. Strap on crampons and harness provided by the certified guide and trek across the ancient glacial ice. Explore crevasses, ice caves, and ash-streaked ice layers — remnants of past volcanic eruptions. The glacier hike takes approximately 3 hours and is suitable for beginners.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to the nearby town of Vík í Mýrdal — Iceland's southernmost village. Explore the dramatic black sand beach of Reynisfjara with its basalt column formations and powerful surf (never turn your back on the waves). Dine in Vík before returning westward toward the resort.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort and pack snacks and a thermos of hot coffee for the road
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or stop at a roadside café near Skógafoss — soup and sandwich (~2,000–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Suður-Vík Restaurant in Vík — cozy spot with fish and chips, lamb burger, or traditional Icelandic plate (~4,500–6,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Glacier hike must be pre-booked with a certified guide — do not attempt without one. Wear warm waterproof layers; crampons and helmets are provided. The South Coast drive is approximately 2.5–3 hours from the Reykjanes area one way — consider an overnight stay in Vík to reduce driving, or start very early.

day_by_day.morning: Leisure morning at the resort. Enjoy a long breakfast and use the resort's hot tub or pool facilities if available. Reflect on the week's adventures and recharge. Do light stretching or yoga — legs may be sore from the glacier hike. Browse local Icelandic craft or souvenir shops near the resort area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir on the Golden Circle route (approx. 1.5 hours from the resort). Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring dating to 1891, set in a geothermal field with bubbling mud pots and steam vents. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this is an authentic and peaceful soak in a truly natural setting.
day_by_day.evening: Soak until closing time and watch the steam rise into the cold January sky. If aurora activity is high, the open geothermal field around the Secret Lagoon offers excellent unobstructed sky views — the ultimate combination of soaking in warm water while watching the Northern Lights overhead. Drive back to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort café or packed snacks for the road
meals.dinner: Stop in Selfoss town on the return drive — try Kaffi Krús for a warm, cozy mid-range dinner with Icelandic fish or lamb (~4,000–6,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Secret Lagoon entry is approximately 3,000–3,500 ISK per adult — much more affordable than the Blue Lagoon. Bring a towel (rentals available) and a dry bag for valuables. The natural surroundings make this feel like a very different, more rustic experience than the Blue Lagoon — both are worth doing.

day_by_day.morning: Mid-trip free morning. Sleep in or take a sunrise walk along the beachfront (sunrise around 11:00 in January). Visit a local geothermal public pool — Icelanders swim outdoors year-round and nearly every town has a community pool with hot pots. Ask the resort for the nearest one for a truly local experience at a fraction of spa prices (~1,000 ISK entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Reykjanes Peninsula — the volcanic peninsula where the resort is located. Visit the Bridge Between Continents (a small footbridge symbolically spanning the Mid-Atlantic Ridge), the Gunnuhver hot spring area with its powerful steam vents and boiling mud pools, and the Reykjanesviti lighthouse on dramatic coastal cliffs.
day_by_day.evening: Second Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep — book a second guided aurora tour for this evening. With seven days in, you now have better aurora forecasting context. Guides will take the group to the darkest, clearest sky locations available on the night. Bring a tripod for long-exposure photography if interested.

meals.breakfast: Lazy resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Café or bakery near the Reykjanes Peninsula — try a traditional Icelandic hot dog (pylsa) from a roadside stand (~500–800 ISK) and a pastry
meals.dinner: Pre-tour dinner at a mid-range restaurant near the resort — fish and chips or a hearty lamb stew to fuel the late night ahead (~4,000–5,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjanes Peninsula is highly geologically active — the area has seen significant volcanic and seismic activity in recent years. Check local advisories on safetravel.is before exploring. Gunnuhver hot springs are impressive but stay on marked paths — ground can be unstable.

day_by_day.morning: Late start after the Northern Lights tour. Brunch at the resort. Pack for an overnight trip to the Snæfellsnes Peninsula — one of Iceland's most diverse and dramatic landscapes, home to the Snæfellsjökull glacier volcano (inspiration for Jules Verne's Journey to the Center of the Earth). Drive north approximately 2.5–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive on the Snæfellsnes Peninsula. Visit Kirkjufell Mountain — Iceland's most photographed mountain — and the adjacent Kirkjufellsfoss waterfall. In winter, with snow and ice, the scene is breathtaking. Continue along the peninsula's northern coast, stopping at Grundarfjörður village.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a mid-range guesthouse or hotel in the Snæfellsnes area (pre-booked). Dine locally and enjoy the remote, peaceful atmosphere. The peninsula's low light pollution makes it excellent for aurora hunting — step outside after dinner and scan the sky.

meals.breakfast: Brunch at the resort before departing
meals.lunch: Stop in Borgarnes town en route — Settlement Center café or a local bakery (~2,500–4,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Bjargarsteinn Mathús in Grundarfjörður — excellent fresh seafood in a cozy harbor-side setting (~5,000–7,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Book Snæfellsnes overnight accommodation well in advance — options are limited in winter. Suggested stay: Hótel Búðir or a guesthouse in Grundarfjörður. The peninsula is approximately 3 hours from the Reykjanes area — an early afternoon departure is ideal.

day_by_day.morning: Full day exploring Snæfellsnes Peninsula. Morning visit to Snæfellsjökull National Park. Walk on the black lava fields at Djúpalónssandur beach — dramatic sea stacks and stone lifting-test boulders used by ancient fishermen. Explore Dritvík cove and the haunting shipwreck remains on the shore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive along the southern coast of the peninsula. Stop at Búðakirkja — the iconic black church set against the glacier and lava fields. Visit Arnarstapi and Hellnar coastal villages connected by a scenic cliffside walking path with sea arches and bird colonies (puffins are gone in winter but the geology is spectacular).
day_by_day.evening: Return to your Snæfellsnes guesthouse. If skies are clear, the remote location offers pristine Northern Lights viewing conditions — some of the darkest skies in Iceland. Wrap up warm and watch from the guesthouse garden or a nearby hillside.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast — typically included or a simple continental spread
meals.lunch: Café Embla in Arnarstapi or a packed lunch from the guesthouse (~2,000–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Return to Grundarfjörður or cook a simple meal at the guesthouse if kitchen facilities are available — pick up groceries at a local Krónan or Nettó (~2,500–4,000 ISK for self-catering)

day_by_day.notes: Weather on Snæfellsnes can change rapidly — the glacier creates its own microclimate. Always check forecasts before heading to the glacier summit or coastal paths. Some coastal paths may be icy — wear crampons or ice grips on boots.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Snæfellsnes Peninsula and drive back south. Stop at Hraunfossar and Barnafoss waterfalls in the Borgarfjörður region — Hraunfossar is a series of rivulets emerging directly from a lava field and flowing into the Hvítá river, stunning in any season. Barnafoss next door is a powerful churning rapid through a narrow canyon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Aegean Bliss Resort on the Reykjanes Peninsula. Check back in, unpack, and do laundry if needed. Rest and recharge at the resort. Visit the resort's spa or hot tub facilities for a relaxing soak after two days of driving and exploring.
day_by_day.evening: Quiet evening at the resort. Review your best photos and Northern Lights footage from the trip. Enjoy dinner at a nearby restaurant. Check aurora forecasts for the remaining nights — you still have three more evenings for potential sightings.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast before departing Snæfellsnes
meals.lunch: Stop at a café in Borgarnes or Akranes en route — fish soup or a warm sandwich (~2,500–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant or a nearby mid-range restaurant — treat yourself to a proper Icelandic lamb rack or Arctic char (~5,500–8,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Snæfellsnes back to Reykjanes is approximately 3–3.5 hours. Road conditions in January can be challenging — check road.is before departing. Fill the fuel tank in Borgarnes as stations become sparse.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to the geothermal town of Hveragerði — located on the Golden Circle route and known for its geothermal greenhouses and hot spring river. Take the Reykjadalur Hot Spring Thermal River hike — a 3 km trail leading to a natural hot river where you can bathe outdoors. The hike takes about 45 minutes each way and the reward is soaking in a steaming river in a snow-dusted valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort and warm up. Visit the Keflavik area for any last-minute shopping — the town has outdoor gear shops, local craft stores, and supermarkets. Pick up Icelandic souvenirs: skyr, Icelandic salt, wool products (lopapeysa sweaters), and lava salt.
day_by_day.evening: Final Northern Lights attempt — drive to a dark coastal area near the resort for an independent aurora watch. Alternatively, book one final guided Super Jeep Northern Lights tour if previous nights were cloudy. The Reykjanes Peninsula's open volcanic landscape offers excellent unobstructed horizon views.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before the Reykjadalur hike
meals.lunch: Café in Hveragerði after the hike — warm soup and freshly baked bread to recover (~2,500–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Mid-range dinner at a Keflavik restaurant — try Olsen Olsen for burgers and local draft beer, or Duus Restaurant for fresh fish (~4,500–6,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjadalur hike is moderate difficulty — the trail can be icy and muddy in January. Wear waterproof hiking boots and bring a change of clothes and a dry bag for your bathing suit. The hot river temperature varies — some sections are very hot, others cooler. Bring a towel.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day in Iceland. Morning leisure at the resort — enjoy a long breakfast, final soak in any resort hot tub or pool facilities, and pack non-essentials. Take a reflective walk along the beachfront, absorbing the raw Icelandic landscape one last time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Reykjavik for a final afternoon in the capital. Visit the Perlan Museum — a stunning glass dome building with exhibits on Iceland's natural wonders including a real ice cave, Northern Lights planetarium show, and volcanic geology displays. Excellent for synthesizing everything you've experienced on the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Reykjavik — splurge slightly on a memorable meal at a quality Icelandic restaurant. Afterward, walk Laugavegur Street one last time, visit a cozy Icelandic bar for a local craft beer, and head back to the resort for a final night. Keep bags packed and set an early alarm if needed.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — enjoy it slowly
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Perlan's café or a nearby Reykjavik spot — open-faced Icelandic sandwiches (smørrebrød-style) or a bowl of skyr with berries (~2,000–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Celebration dinner at Matur og Drykkur in Reykjavik — traditional Icelandic cuisine reimagined with modern technique, using cod's head, lamb, and local herbs (~7,000–10,000 ISK per person — a worthy splurge for the final night)

day_by_day.notes: Perlan Museum entry is approximately 4,500–5,500 ISK — book online in advance to skip queues. The Northern Lights planetarium show inside Perlan is a great consolation if skies were cloudy during the trip, or a wonderful complement if you saw them. Confirm your departure logistics for the next morning.

day_by_day.morning: Departure day. Wake early, enjoy a final resort breakfast. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Drive to Keflavik International Airport (approximately 20–30 minutes from the resort — one of the trip's most convenient logistics). Return rental car if applicable. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in, security, and duty-free shopping.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure from Keflavik. Browse the airport's duty-free for last-minute Icelandic items — Brennivín schnapps, Icelandic chocolates, and cosmetics made from geothermal minerals. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of geothermal soaks, glacier hikes, aurora hunts, and volcanic landscapes.
day_by_day.evening: In-flight or at destination

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast before check-out
meals.lunch: Airport café or restaurant at Keflavik — Icelandic lamb soup or a skyr parfait (~2,500–4,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or at arrival destination

day_by_day.notes: Keflavik Airport is very close to the Reykjanes resort area — one of the great advantages of this accommodation location. Allow extra time if roads are icy or snowy on departure morning. Check your flight status the night before. Icelandic customs allows export of most food items — skyr in sealed containers travels well as a final taste of Iceland.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep
experiences.description: Join a guided super jeep tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from city light pollution for the best chance of witnessing the Aurora Borealis. Expert guides track solar activity and cloud cover to find the clearest skies, and you'll learn about the science and folklore behind the lights.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in Iceland's most iconic milky-blue geothermal pool surrounded by black lava fields. The mineral-rich waters average 38–40°C and are renowned for skin benefits. Book the Comfort package to include a silica mud mask and a drink at the in-water bar.
experiences.best_time_of_day: Evening (for potential northern lights views overhead)

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring dating to 1891 set in a geothermal field with bubbling mud pots and small geysers. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic local experience costs a fraction of the price and feels genuinely wild.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore the colorful streets of downtown Reykjavik with a local guide, sampling traditional Icelandic dishes like skyr, lamb soup (kjötsúpa), fresh langoustine, and rye bread baked in geothermal ground. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church and the Harpa Concert Hall along the way.

experiences.name: Glacier Hike on Sólheimajökull
experiences.description: Strap on crampons and hike across the stunning Sólheimajökull glacier outlet with a certified guide. Marvel at ice caves, crevasses, and vivid blue ice formations while learning about Iceland's glacial geology and climate change. A truly unforgettable physical adventure on the South Coast.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavík International Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check-in, unwind with a welcome drink and light late-night snack prepared by the resort. Brief orientation with concierge about the 13-day program.

meals.breakfast: On board flight
meals.lunch: On board flight
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome snack platter and Icelandic Brennivín schnapps arranged by the resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Ensure private airport transfer is pre-booked. Resort should be notified of late arrival for a warm welcome. Keep Day 1 light — jet lag recovery is essential for the days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late morning start. Enjoy a lavish resort breakfast with panoramic views. Settle into your beachfront suite, explore resort amenities including any on-site geothermal pools or spa facilities. Orientation walk along the beachfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa: Private transfer to the iconic Blue Lagoon (~20 min from most coastal areas near Reykjavik). Soak in the milky-blue geothermal waters surrounded by dramatic black lava fields. Book the premium 'Retreat Spa' package including private changing suite, in-water massage, and silica mud mask ritual.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. Freshen up and enjoy dinner at the resort's signature restaurant. Early night to recover from travel and prepare for adventures ahead.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic luxury breakfast at the resort — skyr parfaits, smoked lamb, fresh pastries, and Icelandic coffee
meals.lunch: Lava Restaurant at Blue Lagoon — premium set menu featuring langoustine soup, pan-seared Arctic char, and Icelandic flatbread
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant — tasting menu with local lamb tenderloin, pan-seared cod, and Icelandic dairy desserts paired with Scandinavian wines

day_by_day.notes: Blue Lagoon must be pre-booked well in advance, especially for premium Retreat packages. Bring a hair conditioner or purchase on-site as the mineral-rich water can be drying.

day_by_day.morning: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour: Private luxury vehicle to Reykjavik city center. Join an exclusive private guided walking tour through the colorful streets of downtown Reykjavik. Sample traditional Icelandic delicacies including hákarl (fermented shark), skyr, pylsur (Icelandic hot dogs), and fresh seafood at local market stalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Reykjavik's cultural highlights: Hallgrímskirkja Church (stunning views from the tower), the Harpa Concert Hall waterfront, and the Sun Voyager sculpture. Browse luxury boutiques on Laugavegur Street for Icelandic wool goods and design items.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep: As darkness deepens (ample darkness in January), join a premium guided super jeep excursion into the Icelandic wilderness far from city light pollution. Expert guides use real-time aurora forecasts to find the best viewing spots. Hot chocolate and Icelandic spirits served under the dancing lights.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet
meals.lunch: Dill Restaurant, Reykjavik — Iceland's first Michelin-starred restaurant offering a Nordic tasting menu with locally foraged and sourced ingredients
meals.dinner: Packed premium thermos of lamb soup and hot cocoa provided by the super jeep tour operator during the Northern Lights hunt; late-night snack at resort upon return

day_by_day.notes: Northern Lights visibility depends on solar activity (Kp index) and cloud cover. January offers very long dark hours (nearly 19 hours of darkness), maximizing aurora chances. Tour operators monitor forecasts daily and may adjust timing.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure — enjoy the resort's spa treatments, in-house geothermal pool, or yoga session if available. Alternatively, take a scenic coastal walk along the beachfront in the crisp January air with views of the North Atlantic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak: Private transfer to Flúðir village (~1.5 hours from Reykjavik area). Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool dating to 1891, set in a geothermal field with bubbling hot springs and steaming geysers nearby. The intimate, natural atmosphere contrasts beautifully with the Blue Lagoon's grandeur.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey via the Golden Circle route (partial), stopping at Geysir geothermal area and Gullfoss waterfall for dramatic winter views illuminated by vehicle headlights and moonlight. Return to resort for a private in-suite dinner experience.

meals.breakfast: In-suite breakfast service — freshly baked Icelandic bread, smoked salmon, scrambled eggs with chives, and Icelandic dairy
meals.lunch: Picnic-style premium lunch prepared by resort chef — thermos of lobster bisque, open-faced smoked trout sandwiches, and Icelandic cheese board enjoyed near the Secret Lagoon
meals.dinner: Private in-suite dining experience arranged by resort — pan-seared reindeer, roasted root vegetables, and skyr panna cotta

day_by_day.notes: Secret Lagoon is far more intimate and less commercialized than Blue Lagoon. January temperatures may be near or below freezing — the contrast of icy air and warm spring water is magical. Book private transfer in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Glacier Hike on Sólheimajökull: Early private luxury transfer to Sólheimajökull glacier outlet on the South Coast (~2.5 hours). Certified glacier guides outfit you with crampons, helmets, and harnesses. Explore the stunning blue-ice formations, crevasses, and ash-streaked glacier surface — a dramatic testament to Iceland's volcanic and glacial landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-hike warm-up at a nearby café. Continue south along the Ring Road to visit Seljalandsfoss and Skógafoss waterfalls — in January these may be partially frozen, creating spectacular ice formations. Photography opportunities are extraordinary.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a premium restaurant in the South Coast region before returning to resort. Keep an eye on aurora forecasts — the South Coast offers excellent dark skies for Northern Lights viewing on the return drive.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast — high-protein options including eggs, smoked meats, and Icelandic oatmeal with berries for energy ahead of the glacier hike
meals.lunch: Warm meal at Skógar Museum café or a pre-arranged premium packed lunch with lamb stew thermos and artisan sandwiches
meals.dinner: Fiskfélagið (Fish Company) or equivalent South Coast premium dining — Arctic char with dill butter, lamb belly, and Icelandic craft beer pairing

day_by_day.notes: Glacier hiking requires moderate fitness. Dress in warm, waterproof layers — the resort concierge can arrange gear rental if needed. January daylight in Iceland is very limited (~5 hours), so timing is critical. Depart early to maximize light.

day_by_day.morning: Full resort relaxation morning. Indulge in a premium spa treatment — hot stone massage, volcanic mud wrap, or couples' treatment if applicable. Enjoy the resort's geothermal pool facilities at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided photography tour of the surrounding coastal landscape. Iceland's January light produces a golden, low-angle glow for several hours — perfect for dramatic landscape photography. A local expert photographer guides you to the most scenic spots near the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep (second attempt): January provides multiple opportunities. Tonight's hunt ventures to a different wilderness location, with the guide selecting the optimal direction based on cloud cover forecasts. Champagne and warm Icelandic spirits served under the aurora.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — smoked lamb, skyr with Icelandic honey, fresh-baked rye bread, and strong Icelandic coffee
meals.lunch: Light resort lunch — lobster bisque, open sandwiches with gravlax, and fresh salads
meals.dinner: Pre-hunt early dinner at resort — hearty Icelandic lamb soup, pan-seared cod with herb crust, and warm lava cake for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Having two Northern Lights excursions planned across the trip significantly improves the odds of a successful sighting. January has exceptional aurora potential due to long dark hours and frequent Kp activity.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Snæfellsnes Peninsula: Private luxury vehicle and guide for a full-day excursion to this magical peninsula (~2 hours from Reykjavik). Visit Snæfellsjökull glacier and national park — the setting of Jules Verne's 'Journey to the Center of the Earth.' Explore dramatic lava fields, sea cliffs, and the iconic Kirkjufell mountain.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Snæfellsnes — visit the charming fishing village of Arnarstapi, the basalt column formations at Lóndrangar, and Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach. The remote, rugged landscape feels otherworldly in winter.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort as darkness falls. Freshen up and enjoy a premium dinner at the resort. If aurora activity is forecast, step out to the beachfront for impromptu Northern Lights viewing directly from the resort grounds.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Private premium picnic arranged by resort — smoked lamb wraps, Icelandic cheese, dried fish, and hot apple cider enjoyed with views of Snæfellsjökull
meals.dinner: Resort fine dining — pan-seared langoustine, slow-braised lamb shank with root vegetable purée, and Icelandic cheese board with cloudberry jam

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes Peninsula is one of Iceland's most scenic regions and often less crowded than the South Coast. Winter driving conditions require a professional driver — private guided transfer is essential.

day_by_day.morning: Reykjavik cultural deep dive: Private transfer to Reykjavik. Visit the National Museum of Iceland for an immersive look at Viking history and Icelandic heritage. Then explore the Settlement Exhibition — an underground museum built around a 10th-century Viking longhouse.
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury shopping along Laugavegur and Skólavörðustígur streets — premium Icelandic wool sweaters (lopapeysa), handcrafted jewelry with Icelandic lava stone, and artisan design items. Visit the Kolaportið flea market for authentic local atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private dinner at one of Reykjavik's finest restaurants, followed by a visit to Reykjavik's vibrant bar scene — the city is famous for its rúntur (pub crawl) culture. Return to resort by private transfer.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Grillið Restaurant at Radisson Blu Saga Hotel — panoramic city views with an Icelandic-Nordic fusion menu
meals.dinner: Matur og Drykkur — celebrated Reykjavik restaurant serving elevated traditional Icelandic cuisine including cod head, lamb heart, and traditional skyr desserts in a beautifully restored warehouse setting

day_by_day.notes: Matur og Drykkur reservations should be made well in advance. The restaurant is beloved for honoring ancient Icelandic recipes with modern technique — a truly unique culinary experience.

day_by_day.morning: Private geothermal wellness morning: Arrange a private geothermal pool session — many luxury hotels and private facilities in Iceland offer exclusive access to natural hot springs. Alternatively, visit Fontana Geothermal Baths at Laugarvatn on the Golden Circle for a premium spa experience with lake views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Golden Circle private tour: Þingvellir National Park (UNESCO World Heritage Site and site of the world's first parliament), Geysir geothermal field (watch Strokkur erupt every 5–10 minutes), and Gullfoss waterfall — possibly Iceland's most dramatic cascade, partially frozen in January.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. Private in-suite romantic dinner or resort restaurant. Stargazing from the beachfront if skies are clear — Iceland's coastal areas offer extraordinary dark skies in January.

meals.breakfast: In-suite breakfast service — freshly squeezed Icelandic berry juice, eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, and warm Icelandic pastries
meals.lunch: Lindin Restaurant at Laugarvatn — intimate lakeside fine dining with Arctic char, wild mushroom risotto, and local lamb
meals.dinner: Resort signature tasting menu with optional wine pairing — seven-course Nordic-inspired menu featuring seasonal and locally sourced ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Þingvellir is also the site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet — a truly geological wonder. In January, the site is serene and largely crowd-free.

day_by_day.morning: Leisure morning at resort. Enjoy a slow breakfast, swim in the resort's geothermal pool, and reflect on the week's adventures. Optional: morning yoga or meditation session on the beachfront (weather permitting) or in a resort studio.
day_by_day.afternoon: Helicopter tour of Iceland's volcanic highlands and glaciers: A truly premium experience — a private helicopter flight over the interior of Iceland, offering aerial views of glaciers, volcanic craters, geothermal steam vents, and black sand deserts. Land on a remote glacier for a champagne toast.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep (third opportunity): Tonight's excursion heads to the Reykjanes Peninsula's remote interior or Landmannalaugar direction for a final premium aurora chase. Expert guides maximize positioning for optimal viewing.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full Icelandic spread with all favorites
meals.lunch: Light resort lunch — lobster rolls, Icelandic fish soup, and fresh salads
meals.dinner: Early pre-excursion dinner at resort — slow-roasted lamb, wild mushroom tart, and warm berry crumble with Icelandic cream

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter tours must be booked well in advance through operators like Norðurflug. Weather-dependent — the concierge should have a backup plan. This is a highlight experience worth every premium investment.

day_by_day.morning: Reykjanes Peninsula exploration: Private guided tour of the geologically dramatic Reykjanes Peninsula — visit the Bridge Between Continents (walk between North American and Eurasian tectonic plates), the Gunnuhver hot springs and mud pools, and the historic Reykjanesviti lighthouse.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final Blue Lagoon visit (optional second visit) or Krauma Geothermal Baths near Reykholt — a more intimate luxury spa experience with five natural geothermal pools and a cold pool, steam room, and relaxation lounge. Enjoy a final soak in Iceland's healing waters.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at resort — celebrate the journey with the resort's finest offerings. Request a special table on the beachfront terrace (with appropriate heating/fire pit setup) for a memorable final evening under Iceland's winter sky.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Premium picnic on the Reykjanes Peninsula — thermos of seafood chowder, artisan bread, and Icelandic cheeses enjoyed near the steaming hot springs
meals.dinner: Resort farewell gala dinner — chef's special tasting menu with Icelandic lobster, lamb, glacier water-poached fish, and a custom dessert celebrating the trip

day_by_day.notes: Krauma Geothermal Baths are fed by Deildartunguhver, Europe's most powerful hot spring. Far less visited than Blue Lagoon, offering an exclusive and peaceful experience.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at resort — leisurely breakfast, last soak in the geothermal pool, and packing. Request a late checkout if available. Stroll the beachfront one final time to absorb the dramatic Icelandic coastal scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Reykjavik for any last-minute shopping, museum visits, or café stops. Visit Kolaportið market or pick up final Icelandic souvenirs — Brennivín spirits, Icelandic sea salt, volcanic chocolate, and wool goods.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Reykjavik before departure preparations. Return to resort or transfer to airport hotel if departing early the following day.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — savor every bite of the Icelandic spread
meals.lunch: Café Loki near Hallgrímskirkja — traditional Icelandic lunch with rye bread ice cream, lamb meat soup, and hákarl for the adventurous
meals.dinner: Apotek Kitchen & Bar, Reykjavik — sophisticated Nordic cuisine in a beautifully restored historic pharmacy building; cocktails with Icelandic botanicals

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with resort in advance. Arrange private transfer to Reykjavik and back. Keep receipts for any VAT refund claims on purchases — Iceland offers tourist VAT refunds on eligible goods.

day_by_day.morning: Final resort morning or airport hotel departure. Enjoy a last Icelandic breakfast. Private luxury transfer to Keflavík International Airport with ample time before departure. Process VAT refunds at the airport if applicable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure from Keflavík International Airport. Relax in the premium airport lounge — Keflavík has a dedicated lounge with Icelandic food and drink offerings. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of aurora hunts, geothermal soaks, glacier hikes, and volcanic landscapes.
day_by_day.evening: In-flight or at destination — carry memories of Iceland's ethereal landscapes, healing waters, and the dancing Northern Lights.

meals.breakfast: Final resort or hotel breakfast, or airport lounge breakfast spread
meals.lunch: Airport lounge or in-flight premium meal service
meals.dinner: In-flight or at final destination

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Keflavík airport at least 2.5–3 hours before international departure. The airport is approximately 45–50 minutes from Reykjavik by private transfer. Pick up any last duty-free Icelandic spirits or chocolates as gifts.

query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January 2026
